aliases: universal arrow from a functor to an object
terminal object of the comma category F ↓ =(c)

evidence.intree_statement: Class UniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) := { arrow_initial : @Initial (=(c) ↓ F); arrow_obj := snd (`1 (@initial_obj _ arrow_initial)); arrow : c ~> F arrow_obj := `2 (@initial_obj _ arrow_initial) }  (the PRIMAL direction only)
"The dual notion, a universal arrow from F to c, is a terminal object of F ↓ =(c)."  (comment only; never formalized)
Definition Cocomma {S : A ⟶ C} {T : B ⟶ C} := @Comma (B^op) (A^op) (C^op) (T^op) (S^op)  (the op-comma infrastructure through which the dual is expressible)

statement_record.book: Dual of the universal arrow: given S : D -> C and c in C, a universal arrow from S to c is a pair <r, v : S r -> c> such that every f : S d -> c factors as f = v ∘ S f' for a unique f' : d -> r.
statement_record.intree: Class UniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) := { arrow_initial : @Initial (=(c) ↓ F); ... } plus the header comment 'The dual notion, a universal arrow from F to c, is a terminal object of F ↓ =(c).'
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the primal direction (from an object to a functor) is formalized, with initiality packaging, ump_universal_arrows, and the left-adjoint assembly AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows. The dual is acknowledged in a comment and is expressible as @UniversalArrow (C^op) (D^op) c (F^op) via the library's definitional duality (C^op^op = C), but no in-tree development names, instantiates, or provides API for it.

aliases: diagonal functor Δ : C ⟶ C ∏ C
product projections universal property (fork / exl / exr / ump_products)
product as right adjoint to the diagonal

evidence.intree_statement: Program Instance Diagonal_Product `(C : Category) : C ⟶ C ∏ C.  (c ↦ (c, c); the binary diagonal; the general Δ into [J, C] is Diagonal at line 33)

ump_products {x y z} (f : x ~> y) (g : x ~> z) (h : x ~> y × z) : h ≈ fork f g ↔ (exl ∘ h ≈ f) * (exr ∘ h ≈ g)  (the pointwise universal property of the projections: unique factorization of any pair f, g through exl, exr)

Program Instance Diagonal_Product_Adjunction (C : Category) `{@Cartesian C} : Diagonal_Product C ⊣ ×(C) := { adj := fun _ _ => {| to := {| morphism := fun f => fst f △ snd f |}; from := {| morphism := fun f => (exl ∘ f, exr ∘ f) |} |} }  (hom-set bijection (Δ x ~> p) ≅ (x ~> ×(C) p) natural in both variables)

statement_record.book: The diagonal functor Δ : C -> C x C sends c to <c, c>; the product projections p : a x b -> a, q : a x b -> b form a universal arrow from Δ to the object <a, b>: any f : c -> a, g : c -> b yield a unique h : c -> a x b with p h = f and q h = g.
statement_record.intree: ump_products : h ≈ fork f g ↔ (exl ∘ h ≈ f) * (exr ∘ h ≈ g), plus Diagonal_Product_Adjunction : Diagonal_Product C ⊣ ×(C) with transposes (f, g) ↦ f △ g and h ↦ (exl ∘ h, exr ∘ h).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the book's pointwise couniversal-arrow property is exactly ump_products (an iff giving existence and uniqueness of the mediating h up to ≈), and the library additionally packages the whole family as the adjunction Δ ⊣ ×(C) with hom-set bijections natural in both variables, whose counit components are the projection pairs (exl, exr). The book's couniversal-arrow PHRASING per se is not used (see maclane:III.1:def3), but the statement content matches up to setoid presentation.

verifier.notes: CONFIRMED. Blind pass independently found the same three witnesses and verified all at the cited lines: Diagonal_Product (Functor/Diagonal.v:46, with the file's lines 59-66 quoting exactly this Mac Lane/Wikipedia statement), ump_products (Structure/Cartesian.v:136, quote exact), Diagonal_Product_Adjunction (Adjunction/Diagonal/Product.v:36-41, quote exact). Blind pass additionally found Adjunction/GAFT/Examples.v diagonal_unique (the unit-direction universal arrow d ~> x(C) in universal_arrow_from_UMP shape), further supporting PRESENT. strength_comparison honestly discloses that the couniversal-arrow PHRASING is deferred to def3's PARTIAL.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition IsKernel {x y k : C} (f : x ~> y) (i : k ~> x) : Type := IsEqualizer f zero_mor k i.  (in Section with Context `{Z : @ZeroObject C})

Lemma kernel_desc {x y k : C} {f : x ~> y} {i : k ~> x} (K : IsKernel f i) {z : C} (h : z ~> x) (Hh : f ∘ h ≈ zero_mor) : ∃! u : z ~> k, i ∘ u ≈ h.  (the universal property in the zero-composite phrasing)
Lemma kernel_monic ... (K : IsKernel f i) : Monic i.

statement_record.book: The kernel of a homomorphism (in Ab, Grp, Rng, R-Mod, ...) is a universal — more exactly, a universal (arrow) for a suitable contravariant functor; the functor is not spelled out in the text.
statement_record.intree: IsKernel f i := IsEqualizer f zero_mor k i, with kernel_desc : any h with f ∘ h ≈ 0 factors uniquely through the kernel inclusion, and kernel_monic.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree captures the universal characterization abstractly and completely for categories with a zero object (kernel = equalizer of f against zero_mor, with unique factorization); intree-weaker relative to the remark's scope: MacLane's contravariant-functor universal also covers his listed Rng, where zero morphisms are unavailable and the kernel is not an equalizer-with-zero, and none of the remark's concrete algebraic categories (Ab, Grp, Rng, R-Mod) exist in-tree to instantiate the notion.

aliases: contravariant power-set functor P : Set^op -> Set
universal element <2, {1}> / subsets classified by characteristic maps
Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets representability (Sub ≅ Hom(-, Ω))

evidence.intree_statement: Class SubobjectClassifier := { Ω : C; truth : 1 ~> Ω; char {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : x ~> Ω; char_pullback : IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one; char_unique : IsPullback h truth u m one → h ≈ char m M }
Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj x |} {| carrier := x ~> Ω |}.  (per-object classification theorem)

Program Definition Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets := {| fobj := fun x : C => {| carrier := SubObj x; ... |}; fmap := ... sub_reindex (unop f) ... |}  (the in-tree contravariant subobject presheaf, the library's counterpart of the power-set functor)

#[export] Program Instance FinSet_Classifier : @SubobjectClassifier FinSet FinSet_Terminal := {| Ω := 2%nat; truth := fun _ => fin_true; char := ... fin_of_bool (fin_existsb (fun a => fin_eqb (m a) b)) |}  (the classical two-valued answer, decidably, on finite sets)

Theorem sets_char_subobject@{o so} {A B : SetoidObject@{o o}} (m : A ~{Sets@{o so}}~> B) (Hm : @Monic Sets@{o so} A B m) : @equiv _ (@SubObj_Setoid Sets@{o so} B) (Build_SubObj ... m ...) (Build_SubObj ... (Sets_Image m) ...)  (with sets_char_pullback line 224 and sets_char_unique line 283: the cross-universe classifier theorems for Sets, truth values in PropSetoid one universe up)

statement_record.book: Find a universal element for the contravariant power-set functor P : Set^op -> Set (classically <2, {1}>: every subset S of X is the preimage of {1} under a unique characteristic function X -> 2).
statement_record.intree: SubobjectClassifier (Ω, truth, char with classifying pullback and uniqueness) with classifier_classifies : SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω) in Sets; instantiated for FinSet with Ω = 2 (FinSet_Classifier); for Sets itself as the cross-universe theorems sets_char_pullback / sets_char_unique / sets_char_subobject with truth-value setoid PropSetoid one universe up; the contravariant Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets presheaf plays the power-set functor's role.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the literal exercise, stronger on generality: the classification content (subobjects of X correspond uniquely to maps X -> Ω with truth pullback) is fully formalized — abstractly, with the classical two-valued answer realized as a genuine instance only over FinSet, and over Sets only as cross-universe theorems (the file proves the truth-value object cannot fit at one universe level, so no one-level universal element of a Sets-valued power-set functor exists there). No power-set functor with a III.1-style universal element is stated as such, and classifier_classifies is per-object rather than the natural isomorphism Sub ≅ Hom(-, Ω) of functors.

gap: Missing pieces relative to the exercise as posed: (1) no power-set functor on Sets/Coq with an III.1-universal-element statement — the content is carried by the subobject-classifier apparatus instead; (2) for Sets the classifier is deliberately NOT an instance (PropSetoid lives one universe up; disclosed size obstruction), so the universal element exists at one level only over FinSet (Ω = 2, finite sets); (3) representability is stated per-object (classifier_classifies), not as a natural isomorphism between the Sub presheaf and Hom(-, Ω).
